# Problem and question — a frozen analytic front end reconstructs as well as a learned one but its codebook is less diverse, and nobody has tested whether token geometry or learning is responsible
## 1. Common ground
EEG tokenizers embed each one-second channel patch with a learned temporal convolution before a Transformer and a vector-quantized codebook (Jiang, 2024) [jiang2024]; when code usage differs between codebooks, the difference is attributed to the reconstruction target (Ma et al., 2025) [maetal2025]; (Cui et al., 2026) [cuietal2026]. Where a front end is not learned, the field's default reading is that it has to be: learnable front ends are proposed because fixed ones are "handmade" (Zeghidour et al., 2021) [zeghidouretal2021].
## 2. Condition
Move: apply-wider. In this project's own runs (topic file; unpublished, one seed each) a frozen filter-bank front end with zero trainable parameters reaches the same tokenizer reconstruction loss as the learned convolution (0.2131 vs 0.2140 over a matched step window) while its codebook perplexity is 27% lower (288 vs 397) — so reconstruction quality does not explain usage. The one account that ties usable codebook dimension to the variance structure of what is quantized was tested only on learned image and speech encoders, by delaying quantization [zhaoetal2026#E2]; the front end was varied in EEG pretraining only without a codebook and without a frozen arm [xieetal2026#E1]. Whether a fixed re-scaling of the tokens (whitening), with no learning in the front end, changes codebook diversity: (no reported number: this is an absence).
## 3. Consequence — So-what ladder
Q1 Why does a frozen filter-bank front end give lower codebook perplexity than a learned convolution at equal reconstruction — token anisotropy, or the absence of training?
  → because Q1 is unanswered, Q2 cannot be answered: can an analytic, interpretable front end serve a discrete-token EEG model without being trained?        evidence: open debate D_draft_FixedVsLearnedFrontend ([zeghidouretal2021], [andersonetal2023] vs [schlutergutenbrunner2022]); a fixed band front end is already used in front of VQ tokenizers with no usage reported [sukhbaataretal2026]; "rethinking the signal reconstruction target", e.g. with a fixed scattering transform, is named as future work [barmpasetal2025].
  → Q3 Are the code-usage differences reported between EEG tokenizers properties of the target or of the geometry of the quantizer's input?        evidence: [maetal2025] and [cuietal2026] report opposite goals for usage on the same corpus and explain the difference by the target (D_draft_TargetMatters; conflict not stated by either paper).
## 4. Three-step sentence
I am studying the codebook of an EEG tokenizer under a frozen filter-bank front end and under a learned convolution because I want to find out why equal reconstruction comes with unequal codebook perplexity, in order to help readers who design EEG foundation models understand whether an interpretable front end must be trained to feed a discrete codebook.
## 5. Research question
Can the codebook perplexity deficit of a frozen filter-bank front end against a learned convolution in an EEG tokenizer be at least halved without training the front end by a fixed whitening of its tokens, and does whitening gain more than rank-matched noise does?
(A whether question. Yes: an analytic front end needs a fixed normalisation stage, not gradients, to feed a discrete codebook, and the gradient starvation of structured front ends can be set aside for tokenization. No: flattening the token spectrum is not enough, and what a trained front end supplies has to be looked for elsewhere. Earlier wording, changed after the blind restatement because no arm trains the bank: "Why does a frozen filter-bank front end that reconstructs as well as a learned convolution give lower codebook perplexity in an EEG tokenizer: is the deficit set by the anisotropy of its tokens, which a fixed whitening removes without any training, or by the absence of a trained front end?")

## 7. Key terms
frozen filter-bank front end · learned convolution · whitening · codebook perplexity · rank-matched noise
## 8. Definitions
- **frozen filter-bank front end** — `PureDynFrontEnd` of the project code with n_ap = 48 real poles, K = 8 damped oscillators, 4 time bins, band 0.5–90 Hz, phase channels on: a 256-dimensional token of pooled log energies and demodulated phases, zero trainable parameters. Other definitions: fixed FFT band masks [sukhbaataretal2026]; mel filterbank [schlutergutenbrunner2022]. This one because it is the configuration whose deficit the project record documents.
- **learned convolution** — LaBraM's three-block temporal convolution (576 parameters) producing a 256-dimensional token [jiang2024].
- **whitening** — a fixed affine map applied to the frozen front end's token t: t' = s · C_shrunk^(-1/2) (t − m), with mean m and covariance C estimated once from 20,000 training patches, C_shrunk = 0.9 C + 0.1 (tr C / 256) I, and the scalar s set so that the mean squared norm of t' equals that of t. Buffers only; no gradient reaches it. Other definitions: per-channel energy normalisation (PCEN) in audio [zeghidouretal2021] — a learned compression; not used here because it has parameters.
- **codebook perplexity** — exp of the entropy of the histogram of codes assigned to 20,000 held-out validation patches, computed at steps 10,000, 12,000, 14,000 and 16,000; the outcome is the mean of the four (the EMA usage the quantizer keeps is logged beside it). Other definitions: utilisation = share of codes used at least once [guoetal2024], [fangetal2025]; per-batch usage [fifty2025]. Perplexity because utilisation saturates near 5% for every arm in the project record and hides differences.
- **rank-matched noise** — Gaussian noise added to the frozen front end's tokens, isotropic in the 256 dimensions, with the variance at which the tokens' participation-ratio effective rank (centred covariance, 8,800 held-out patches) equals that of the whitened tokens. It raises rank without rescaling any direction the bank already had.
